tasks.instruction: The function should return a record whose first field is the smaller input and whose second field is the larger input.
tasks.note: Low field picked with the wrong arm of the select.

tasks.instruction: The function should return the median of its three inputs (the middle value once sorted).
tasks.note: Median as max(min(a,b), min(max(a,b),c)); the start has min and max exchanged in both inner and outer calls.

tasks.instruction: The function subtracts the second input from the first, giving 0 when that would go below zero; the result must be capped at 255 instead of 1000.
tasks.note: Three-way select: floor 0, cap, or the difference.

tasks.instruction: Return 0 for scores below 50, 1 for 50 through 69, 2 for 70 through 89, and 3 for 90 or more.
tasks.note: Select chain with four outcomes; the 70 boundary is wrong at the start.

tasks.instruction: The function returns an ordering code (0 less, 1 equal, 2 greater) and a flag; the flag should be true exactly when the inputs are equal.
tasks.note: Flag must agree with the equal branch of the code.

tasks.instruction: Return the 4-bit field held in bits 4 through 7 of the input.
Replace bits 8 through 15 of the first input with the low 8 bits of the second input; no other bits may change.
tasks.note: The second input must be masked before shifting.

tasks.instruction: Return the index and value of the largest element of the array; when several elements tie for largest, report the first one.
tasks.note: Strict comparison keeps the first maximum; an all-zero array reports index 0.

tasks.instruction: Add the third input to the array element at the given index and cap it at 1000; the cap must also apply when the addition wraps around past 2^32.
tasks.note: Wrap detected as sum below the old element.

tasks.instruction: Return true only when all three inputs are different from each other.
tasks.note: First and third inputs were never compared.

tasks.instruction: The function should compute three times the first input plus the second (wrapping), then flip bits with 0x5A.
Hash all four elements: start from 7 and, for each element in order, multiply the state by 31 and add the element, wrapping.
tasks.note: Fold count must cover every element.

tasks.instruction: Return the three inputs sorted ascending as a record; the current version can leave the first two fields out of order.
tasks.note: Missing third compare-exchange of the sorting network.

tasks.instruction: When the record's flag is true add the second input to its value (wrapping); otherwise subtract it, stopping at 0 instead of wrapping below zero.
tasks.note: Floor at zero missing on the subtract path.

tasks.instruction: Return true when the first record beats the second: the larger value wins, and on equal values the first wins only if its flag is set and the second's flag is not.
tasks.note: Tie-break must look at both flags.

tasks.instruction: Return the minimum and maximum of all four array elements as a record, minimum first.
tasks.note: Fourth element was never read; index 4 wraps to 0.
